scope: New interoperability implementation and its published contracts; not a fresh whole-repository or SaaS review

dimensions.name: Correctness and mathematical contracts
dimensions.reason: All four defects have regression coverage, including exact numeric metadata and signed-zero closure. Wider unsupported variants remain explicit.

dimensions.name: Architecture and maintainability
dimensions.reason: Native dependencies are isolated in optional adapters; a build gate prevents leakage into core. Geometry allocations share a budget across rows.

dimensions.name: Validation and test evidence
dimensions.reason: Pinned GDAL 3.13.3 independently verifies nine TIFFs, CF and XYZ semantics; mask precedence and malformed mask regressions pass. Six Linux containment cases and a real native workload pass.

dimensions.name: Documentation and contract clarity
dimensions.reason: Contracts identify optional dependencies, tested subsets, runtime versions, OS limits and remaining exclusions.

dimensions.name: Delivery and operational readiness
dimensions.reason: Windows and Linux resource limits are measured. Linux additionally verifies read-only root, disabled networking and an unprivileged native workload. Hosted service deployment/load acceptance remains separate.

findings.title: GeoPackage geometry registration can disagree with decoded features
findings.trigger: Change the pinned XYZ LINESTRING fixture registration to POINT with z=0 and m=0. The decoder still returns both XYZ lines.
findings.impact: Consumers cannot rely on the declared geometry schema; source metadata and returned values contradict one another without a diagnostic.
findings.action: Read geometry_type_name, z and m; enforce permitted geometry subtype/dimensions for every non-null geometry. Validate registered SRS consistency. Add positive generic-GEOMETRY and negative type/dimension cases.
findings.resolution: Registered geometry type, Z/M policy and SRS consistency are checked; generic GEOMETRY and optional dimensions retain valid inputs.

findings.title: A missing registered geometry column is silently accepted
findings.trigger: Register absent_geom against a table containing only id. geoPackage returns a successful GeoPackageFeatures with no geometry values.
findings.impact: The explicit one-geometry-column contract is not enforced; malformed database metadata looks like a successfully decoded feature table.
findings.action: Check the selected schema contains exactly the registered geometry column before reading rows, including empty tables. Reject missing/mismatched columns before returning success.
findings.resolution: The selected schema must contain the registered geometry column, including empty tables.

findings.title: Zarr version validation truncates fractional numbers
findings.trigger: An otherwise ordinary one-cell array with zarr_format=2.5 decodes value 42 successfully.
findings.impact: Invalid metadata is admitted as version 2. This repeats the numeric narrowing problem previously fixed elsewhere in the engine.
findings.action: Require a JSON number representing an exact integer equal to 2, before any narrowing. Test fractions, strings, booleans, huge exponents and valid 2.
findings.resolution: Zarr version must be numeric and exactly integral before conversion. Fractional/string/boolean/overflow cases reject.

findings.title: Polygon closure compares signed-zero representations instead of coordinates
findings.trigger: A triangular WKB ring begins at (+0,0) and closes at (-0,0). Hexplain reports Unclosed polygon ring; Shapely reports the same ring valid and closed.
findings.impact: A numerically closed geometry is rejected because Kotlin list equality distinguishes boxed Double signed zeros.
findings.action: Compare ordinates numerically after nonfinite validation; preserve source coordinates. Add both signed-zero closure cases and a genuinely unclosed control.
findings.resolution: Ring endpoints compare numeric ordinates, preserving signed-zero representations while accepting numeric closure.

findings.title: Collected-byte limits do not bound native or geometry memory
findings.trigger: HDF metadata/dataFlat and JDBC values may allocate before adapter accounting; GeoPackage geometry allocation is additional to raw blob accounting.
findings.impact: The published 64 MiB limits are not a process-memory guarantee. No exploit or production exposure is claimed: the adapters are currently offline.
findings.action: Use an optional adapter module and a worker with OS-enforced memory/time limits; add aggregate geometry budgets and native allocation stress tests before connecting uploads.
findings.resolution: Offline adapters have shared geometry budgets and pre-execution Windows/Linux OS limits. Six Linux tests verify OOM, process count, deadline, read-only filesystem and disabled networking. Real HDF5/Parquet/GeoPackage/TIFF execution passes as an unprivileged user under 512 MiB with swap disabled. Hosted route integration remains a separate acceptance task.

findings.title: Storage-order decoding does not establish geospatial semantic parity
findings.trigger: NetCDF lacks CF/record handling, HDF-EOS axis mapping rejects, and transform/mask helpers do not extract metadata from files.
findings.impact: 611 pixel matches cannot be interpreted as coordinate, CRS, nodata, alpha or mask equivalence. Companion references are valuable but do not replace the missing GDAL comparisons.
findings.action: Run selected-variable and feature comparisons against a functioning pinned GDAL runtime; compare complete values, geometry ordinates, axis mapping, geotransforms and masks independently.
findings.resolution: The requested selected-variable/feature comparisons now run against pinned GDAL 3.13.3: nine TIFFs, one CF variable and two XYZ features. Every pixel, transform and mask is compared. Byte alpha and one full-resolution internal TIFF mask now decode with tested precedence over nodata/alpha. Broader HDF-EOS/CF, external masks and custom CRS remain explicit capability exclusions.

findings.title: Offline native adapters become dependencies of every core consumer
findings.trigger: jHDF, SQLite JDBC and DuckDB JDBC are implementation dependencies in core/build.gradle.kts, despite not being exposed through hosted decoding.
findings.impact: All consumers inherit native packaging/platform and update obligations even when they need only the native parser or compiler.
findings.action: Move library-backed adapters and their probes into an optional module with an explicit capability boundary; keep native codecs independently usable.
findings.resolution: jHDF, SQLite and DuckDB are optional adapters dependencies. verifyCoreIsolation checks core runtime resolution excludes all three.

decision: All seven findings are addressed within the reviewed offline adapter contracts. Linux containment and pinned GDAL semantic acceptance are measured. This does not certify all GDAL formats or a deployed hosted service.
